chat.author: Jen Linkova
chat.text:
From Robert Sparks: ""Hedgedoc, which is the software behind notes.ietf.org, has had an issue
for some time with a client losing its connection, but not telling the
user about it. The result is someone can be typing along for quite some
time and as far as they can tell, notes.ietf.org has captured their
work, but no one else can see it and the local work will disappear on a
shift-reload.
The hedgedoc maintainers have been trying to issue a release that would
at least tell the user when this was happening, but they've had to pull
two attempts made last week already for additional issues the releases
introduced.
What this means for IETF 127:
The best option is to ask your note-takers to take notes offline and
paste them into notes.ietf.org, and mail them to the list, later.
Otherwise, if collaborative note taking is important to your groups,
have a dedicated volunteer watching to see if expected updates aren't
appearing and have them nudge the contributors to reconnect with a shift
reload. If your notetakers are comfortable watching the browser's
console, they _might_ see a message when the connection is noted to be
failed.
If a new release appears and passes basic tests, we'll do an emergency
upgrade, but at this point I do not think it is likely that this will
happen.
What this means going forward:
We're planning to shift which system we use for collaborative
note-taking going forward. The current plan is to shift to wiki.js as
soon as the collaborative editing feature is released there."
